chapter_title: The Human is less than all the Things of the Universe, and he is rebellious beyond them all.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic reminiscence (Mani-on-the-road scene) and polemical/ethical application against humanity’s blasphemy, followed by later catechetical lists (“five” and “three”). The oldest recoverable substrate appears only as embedded cosmological kernels (Light/Darkness mechanics; aeons; descent to the province of death; eschatological binding; Cross of Light as a cosmic presence).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic travel-setting about “the apostle” with narrative staging; no systematic cosmos→cosmos mapping.

Continuation of the anecdotal scene and illustrative comparison (mountain vs. gathered flesh). Embedded speech, but still a worldly illustration within a biography-like frame, not the impersonal cosmological system-exposition of the substrate.
Moralizing comparison (mountains/seas silent vs. humanity blaspheming) and anti-theodicy polemic (“no cause of evil after God”); application content rather than cosmological degree-structure.
Polemical denunciation of humanity attributing rulers/demons to God; accusatory voice and ethical/theological disputation, not systematic correspondential cosmology.
Dialogue/Q&A apparatus (“one of his disciples… Tell us, our master”): classic Kephalaia frame layer.
Explicit NT passion complex (cross, enemies, torment/shame) used as argument; this enters via Christian narrative tradition rather than the pre-compilation cosmological substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Jesus did not come and s[a]ve the world because of mankind alone, but [ ... he] came and revealed on earth [ ... ] was strong outside in [ ... ] And [whe]n he had finished doing his [t]ask outside [i]n the great u[ni]verse, he came [ ... he wen]t further with Adam and Eve and revealed [to them].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution “[The ap]ostle [says] to him:” (frame). Removed the catechetical/institutional extension “Even so, he sent the apostles… generation by generation… revealed… five great thin[gs]” as later church-facing summary rather than substrate cosmology.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Kernel is cosmological-task language (Jesus operating “outside… in the great u[ni]verse,” revelation to Adam and Eve) consistent with Manichaean cosmic hierarchy; surrounding dialogue frame and apostolic-mission/catechetical pivot are later.

paragraphs.core_text: they belong to the race of ligh[t].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical list label and reporting clause (“[Firs]t: He told them that…”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: “race of ligh[t]” is a cosmological-anthropological identity claim; its packaging as a numbered apostolic teaching-item suggests later catechetical editing.

paragraphs.core_text: the aeons [of the greatness], how they occur; and [the manner of] the darkness, how it t[o]o exists.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the list label/reporting verbs (“[Se]cond: He unveiled to them… and he taught them…”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct cosmological content (aeons of greatness; Darkness as an ontological domain) fits the substrate’s internal cosmic system; numbered catechesis is later scaffolding.

paragraphs.core_text: the [l]ight great-[ness], how it has been active against the pow[er of] darkness and conquered it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the list label/reporting clause (“[The th]ird time: He proclaimed to them about the…”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Light-vs-Darkness mechanics (“active… conquered”) is core cosmological teaching; the didactic list format likely reflects later catechetical arrangement.

paragraphs.core_text: he came to the province of death [ ... ... ] that is flesh, until he should find profit and bring them from the gate of the underworld below, for [they had] been swa[ll]owed into it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the list label/reporting clause (“Fourth: He taught them that…”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological descent/rescue schema (province of death; underworld gate; swallowing) reads like substrate mechanism; list packaging is secondary.

paragraphs.core_text: the rebels shall be bound in a great fetter
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the list label and editorial application (“Fifth: He explained to us that…”; and the specification tied to proclamation “by the apostle”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological binding motif can belong to the older cosmic judiciary; explicit linkage to what is “proclaimed by the apostle” is a later authority-anchor.
Frame marker plus community category (“All the faithful who believe…”) introducing a catechetical triad; this is church-facing instruction, not impersonal system description.
Catechetical identity for “the faithful” in virtue/faith terms; no cosmic degree mapping or mechanism.
Institutional loyalty/authority (“believed the apostle who has been manifested”) and blessing language; later community catechesis.

paragraphs.core_text: the Cross of Light, which g[rie]ves in the totality, being present in what is visible and what is not vis[ib]le.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ethical-instruction clause (“They a[ct] with restraint and charity to…”), retaining the cosmological description of the Cross of Light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening is pastoral ethics (restraint/charity) aimed at community behavior, but the tail is a cosmological statement about the Cross of Light as a pervasive reality spanning visible/invisible—an older kernel embedded in later exhortation.
